nodes.summary: The independence-model weight for `xs` and `ys` (Durbin et al., chapter 4): `η² (1 - η)^(|xs| + |ys|) ∏ q xs ∏ q ys`. This is a probability when `q` is a normalized nonnegative distribution and `0 < η < 1`, as required by `LinearGapLogOdds`.
nodes.title: Independence-model weight of a sequence pair

nodes.summary: The state that emits an alignment column: `M` for `(some a, some b)`, `X` for `(some a, none)`, `Y` for `(none, some b)` (and `M`, unused, for the invalid `(none, none)`).

nodes.summary: The pair HMM's transition weights do not depend on the current state: every transition into an emitting state `s` (from the begin state or from any emitting state) has weight `π s`, and every transition into the end state has weight `τ`.

nodes.summary: The sum over all alignments of `xs` and `ys` of the joint weight of the sequences and the alignment.

nodes.summary: The total weight `P(xs, ys)` of a pair HMM: the total weight of all state paths that emit `xs` and `ys` (`likelihood_eq_sum`), by the first-column recursion.
nodes.title: Total weight of a sequence pair under a pair HMM

nodes.summary: The hypotheses of the log-odds correspondence: a memoryless pair HMM with normalized positive transition and emission probabilities, normalized positive background frequencies and `0 < η < 1`, whose per-column log-odds scores against the independence model are the integer scores `σ a b` (aligned pair) and `gap` (gap column).
nodes.title: Hypotheses of the linear-gap log-odds correspondence

nodes.summary: For a memoryless pair HMM, the log-odds of an alignment against the independence model is its linear-gap alignment score plus `log (τ / η²)`.
nodes.title: Log-odds of one alignment

nodes.summary: For a memoryless pair HMM whose per-column log-odds scores are `σ a b` and `gap`, the log-odds Viterbi score against the independence model is the Needleman–Wunsch score with substitution scores `σ` and linear gap score `gap`, plus the length term `log (τ / η²)`.
nodes.title: Log-odds Viterbi is linear-gap Needleman–Wunsch

Mathematical Biology

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
